subject: problems installing stan on windows xp

messages.subject: problems installing stan on windows xp
parts:
Hi,

I seem to be cursed. I'm trying to install stan on a windows xp machine. Right from the start i'm having problems. Just for starters (i did an install of the latest Rtools, with no apparent problems) , the inital extraction falls over

$ tar -xzf --no-same-owner st*tgz
tar (child): --no-same-owner: Cannot open: No such file or directory
tar (child): Error is not recoverable: exiting now
tar: Child returned status 2
tar: Error is not recoverable: exiting now


but anyway this seems to work
$ tar -xzf st*tgz

and so does this

$ make bin/libstan.a
g++ -I src -I lib/eigen_3.1.1 -I lib/boost_1.51.0 -O3 -Wall -Wno-unused-function -Wno-uninitialized   -c -o bin/stan/agrad/agrad.o src/stan/agrad/agrad.cpp
g++ -I src -I lib/eigen_3.1.1 -I lib/boost_1.51.0 -O3 -Wall -Wno-unused-function -Wno-uninitialized   -c -o bin/stan/math/matrix.o src/stan/math/matrix.cpp
g++ -I src -I lib/eigen_3.1.1 -I lib/boost_1.51.0 -O3 -Wall -Wno-unused-function -Wno-uninitialized   -c -o bin/stan/agrad/matrix.o src/stan/agrad/matrix.cpp
In file included from src/stan/agrad/matrix.cpp:4:0:
src/stan/agrad/matrix.hpp: In static member function ‘static double stan::agrad::<unnamed>::dot_product_vv_vari::var_dot(stan::agrad::vari**, stan::agrad::vari**, size_t)’:
src/stan/agrad/matrix.hpp:689:31: warning: comparison between signed and unsigned integer expressions
ar -rs bin/libstan.a bin/stan/agrad/agrad.o bin/stan/math/matrix.o bin/stan/agrad/matrix.o
ar: creating bin/libstan.a


but then
$ make bin/stanc
make: *** No rule to make target `bin/stanc'.  Stop.


so try

$ make bin/stanc.exe
g++ -I src -I lib/eigen_3.1.1 -I lib/boost_1.51.0 -O3 -Wall -Wno-unused-function -Wno-uninitialized   -c -o bin/stan/command/stanc.o src/stan/command/stanc.cpp
In file included from src/stan/gm/compiler.hpp:6:0,
                 from src/stan/command/stanc.cpp:2:
src/stan/gm/parser.hpp:145:5: internal compiler error: Segmentation fault
Please submit a full bug report,
with preprocessed source if appropriate.
See <http://gcc.gnu.org/bugs.html> for instructions.
makefile:74: recipe for target `bin/stan/command/stanc.o' failed
make: *** [bin/stan/command/stanc.o] Error 1

Any help, clues would be appreciated.

Thanks

Mark

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: problems installing stan on windows xp
parts:
On Thursday, October 11, 2012 5:41:36 AM UTC-4, Marko wrote:
so try 

$ make bin/stanc.exe
This is the correct make target on Windows.

g++ -I src -I lib/eigen_3.1.1 -I lib/boost_1.51.0 -O3 -Wall -Wno-unused-function -Wno-uninitialized   -c -o bin/stan/command/stanc.o src/stan/command/stanc.cpp
In file included from src/stan/gm/compiler.hpp:6:0,
                 from src/stan/command/stanc.cpp:2:
src/stan/gm/parser.hpp:145:5: internal compiler error: Segmentation fault
Please submit a full bug report,
with preprocessed source if appropriate.
See <http://gcc.gnu.org/bugs.html> for instructions.
makefile:74: recipe for target `bin/stan/command/stanc.o' failed
make: *** [bin/stan/command/stanc.o] Error 1

My first guess with all of these is that the machine ran out of memory. You can watch memory consumption while it is compiling with Task Manager. It may be possible to increase what I believe is called "virtual memory" in Windows XP and is called a "swap file" by everyone else.

You can also try to throttle back on the optimization. Although we recommend that *models* be compiled at O3, whether the *parser* is compiled with optimization doesn't make much difference. So, maybe

$ make O=2 bin/stanc.exe

works, and if not then try O=1 and O=0. Although a while back, we were having a problem where the parser would build with higher levels of optimization but not lower levels. My guess is that you will run into more problems later. But this might get you one step closer and you may be able to do some models.

We don't test regularly on Windows XP or any 32bit system, although Jiqiang did get Stan to build on his Windows XP laptop a few months ago.

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: problems installing stan on windows xp
parts:
On Saturday, October 13, 2012 11:48:14 PM UTC-4, Marko wrote:
Thanks for the response Ben, but it seems like memory is not the issue (watching the task manager) showed that it never consumed more than 2.5G, out of a total of 3.6), Also reducing the optimization levels made no difference either. So, i guess its off the install it on our linux machine.

If you want to keep trying on Windows, there are a few choices. Is this 32bit? If so, the problem might be address space. You can increase that somewhat by following the instructions here

http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/bb613473%28VS.85%29.aspx

A while back, Daniel was building Stan with mixed success on Windows 7 with Virtual Studio (not sure which version). You can also try installing clang (which is much less compiler-intensive) for Windows. There are instructions for building it from source on the clang website, or some guy on the internet put Windows binaries (use at your own risk) here

http://sourceforge.net/projects/mingw-w64/files/Toolchains%20targetting%20Win64/Personal%20Builds/rubenvb/clang-3.1-release/

If that works, you just need to specify CC=clang++ when you execute make.

Ben
